items.subject: english-literature-aqa
items.title: Characters: Sheila, Eric, Gerald and Mrs Birling
items.reason: The video teaches a fabricated direct quote for Eric ('he's been here and we all know what we did') and incorrectly claims Mrs Birling is the only character who never accepts responsibility (ignoring Mr Birling).

mark_affecting.quote: He says, 'he's been here and we all know what we did.'
Mrs Birling is the only character who never accepts any responsibility.

items.subject: science-aqa
items.title: Electromagnetic Induction and Transformers
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims that using a stronger magnet increases the frequency of the generator output, which would lose marks on a GCSE exam.

mark_affecting.quote: If you spin that generator faster, or if you swap in a stronger magnet, you actually get a dual effect... the frequency of the output goes up too

items.subject: science-aqa
items.title: Magnets, Electromagnetism and the Motor Effect
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims permanent magnets are made of iron, which contradicts the core GCSE distinction between soft iron (temporary/electromagnets) and steel/alloys (permanent magnets) and would lose marks in an exam.

mark_affecting.quote: They produce their own permanent magnetic field and are usually made of specific materials, like iron, steel, nickel or cobalt.

items.subject: classical-civilisation-ocr
items.title: Death & Burial
items.reason: The video incorrectly instructs students that the coin could be placed on the eyes rather than solely in the mouth, which risks losing marks on specification recall questions.

mark_affecting.quote: placed inside the mouth or resting on the eyes of the deceased

items.subject: classical-civilisation-ocr
items.title: Foundation Myths: Athens & Rome
items.reason: The video incorrectly attributes the founding of Alba Longa to Aeneas instead of his son Ascanius (Aeneas founded Lavinium), which would cost marks on foundation sequence questions in GCSE Classical Civilisation.

mark_affecting.quote: Aeneas flees west, and eventually founds a settlement in Italy called Alba Longa.

items.subject: classical-civilisation-ocr
items.title: Journeying to the Underworld
items.reason: The video incorrectly presents Persephone's time division as an equal half-year seasonal split (spring/summer vs autumn/winter) rather than the prescribed Homeric Hymn's one-third below and two-thirds above, and attributes Virgil's 100-year wait to lacking an obol rather than being unburied.

mark_affecting.quote: She now splits her year: spring and summer above ground with her mother... and autumn and winter below ground as queen of the underworld

If you didn't have this exact coin, the obol, placed on your body when you were buried, your soul was literally stranded on the muddy riverbank of the Acheron for a hundred agonizing years before Charon would finally take you across for free.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Russia in 1894: Economy and Society
items.reason: The video prominently states in audio and on-screen graphics that only 14% (one in seven) of the empire were ethnic Russians, which is severely inaccurate compared to the census figure of roughly 44% ('fewer than half').

mark_affecting.quote: only about one in seven, yeah just 14% were actually ethnic Russians

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: War Communism, Kronstadt and the NEP
items.reason: The video states that the 1921–22 Volga famine was caused by losing Ukraine under the 1918 Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, giving students an incorrect cause and anachronistic sequence for an examined syllabus topic.

mark_affecting.quote: and losing Ukraine's grain belt from the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, this huge drop in farming triggered a catastrophic famine in the Volga region in 1921 and 1922

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Terror, Purges and the Cult of Stalin
items.reason: The video states that five of eight Red Army marshals were executed (there were only five marshals, three of whom were shot) and claims Trotsky was airbrushed out of photos of Lenin's funeral (he was absent from the funeral).

mark_affecting.quote: Five of the Red Army's eight marshals? Executed.
Five of the Red Army's eight marshals? Executed.
Trotsky was famously airbrushed out of pictures of Lenin's funeral.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: The Great Patriotic War, 1941-1945
items.reason: The video states that Stalin signed the German surrender in Berlin on 9 May 1945, whereas Stalin signed nothing and Marshal Zhukov signed for the Soviet Union.

mark_affecting.quote: That push, ultimately ended with Stalin signing the German surrender in Berlin on the 9th of May 1945, which became Victory Day.

items.subject: drama-aqa
items.title: Performance Interpretation: Rani Standing Her Ground
items.reason: The video explicitly claims Abdul 'doesn't speak English' upon arriving at Windsor Castle (03:22), which contradicts the set text and would cause a student to lose marks for textual inaccuracy in their exam.

mark_affecting.quote: Just picture his arrival at Windsor Castle. He doesn't speak English, and he is acutely aware of how much he stands out.

items.subject: drama-aqa
items.title: Plot and Structure: A Tale Across Two Countries
items.reason: The video incorrectly names the central Tanaka family as the 'Hashimoto family' multiple times and provides an incorrect premiere sequence for the production history.

mark_affecting.quote: On the other, we have the Hashimoto family, desperately searching in Japan.
This is the kind of work typical of venues like the Tricycle Theatre, where the play actually premiered, and then the National Theatre's Dorfman stage.

items.subject: drama-aqa
items.title: Characters: The Hashimoto Family and Their Captors
items.reason: The video incorrectly identifies Kum-Chol as an officer/captor overseeing Hanako rather than her husband in North Korea, which would cost marks on character and relationship questions.

mark_affecting.quote: Take Kum-Chol, the officer. He's complicit, sure...

items.subject: drama-aqa
items.title: Dramatic Methods: Cross-Cutting and Stage Directions
items.reason: F9 is mark-affecting because claiming English stands in for Japanese and Korean is stylized directly misrepresents the set text script, which explicitly uses phonetic Japanese and Korean dialogue before shifting to English.

mark_affecting.quote: Now, in this play, English is used to stand in for Japanese, which is Hanako's mother tongue. But over in North Korea, she is forced to adopt a stylized Korean.

items.subject: drama-aqa
items.title: Practitioner Application: Documentary Theatre and Brecht
items.reason: The video incorrectly refers to the play's central family and home as the 'Hashimoto family' / 'Hashimoto household' instead of the Tanaka family, which would cause students to lose marks in exam questions on character and staging.

mark_affecting.video_says: emotional journey of the Hashimoto family
design of the Hashimoto household in the Japan scenes
mark_affecting.lesson_says: The Tanaka Household: Where Documentary Meets Domestic / the Tanaka family

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: The Great American Desert and Manifest Destiny
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims President Polk doubled the size of the United States, conveying an inaccurate historical figure.

mark_affecting.quote: took less than five years for President Polk to double the size of the United States all over again

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: The Civil War: Impact on Civilians
items.reason: The video claims 200,000 women entered the federal civil service or wartime nursing (F25), which is an order of magnitude error that could cost marks on quantitative evidence in an exam answer.

mark_affecting.quote: Something like 200,000 women entered the federal civil service or wartime nursing

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Mountain Meadows and the Mormon Question
items.reason: The video repeats the uncorrected claim that the murdered Mormon leader was killed in Missouri rather than Arkansas, misrepresenting the causal suspicion directed at the Arkansas wagon train.

mark_affecting.quote: connected to the past murder of a Mormon leader back in Missouri

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Carpetbaggers, the Klan and the End of Reconstruction
items.reason: F29 teaches incorrect historical voter statistics and dates misattributed to Mississippi rather than Louisiana.

mark_affecting.quote: In 1880, there were roughly 130,000 registered Black voters... by the year 1900, that number had plummeted to under 1,000.

items.subject: drama-aqa
items.title: Themes: Class, Motherhood, Race, Sexuality
items.reason: The video incorrectly states in voiceover and on the timeline slide that the Notting Hill race riots occurred before the play's premiere, reversing the historical chronological sequence.

mark_affecting.quote: Literally weeks before the curtain went up in 1958, the Notting Hill race riots completely shocked the country [and on slide: Notting Hill race riots occur before premiere]

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: The League of Nations: Structure and Membership
items.reason: The video states that the League's Geneva headquarters opened on 10 January 1920 rather than November 1920, which directly contradicts the lesson's mark scheme and practice answer.

mark_affecting.quote: The whole machine was officially switched on and came to life on January 10th, 1920, when the League's brand new headquarters opened its doors over in Geneva, Switzerland.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Détente, SALT 1 and the Nixon-Brezhnev Era
items.reason: F77 is mark-affecting because the video teaches an incorrect cause and sequence, claiming Nixon's China trip prompted Brezhnev to agree to the Moscow summit within three months, whereas the summit had already been agreed in October 1971.

mark_affecting.quote: So within just three months of Nixon's China trip, Brezhnev agreed to host Nixon in Moscow.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Spring Offensive, Hundred Days and Armistice
items.reason: The video presents the old, reversed sequence and false causation where Haig's 'backs to the wall' order (11 April) causes the appointment of Foch as Generalissimo (26 March), which would cost marks on exam questions covering the Allied unified command.

mark_affecting.quote: In response to this terrifying German advance, British commander Haig issues his famous 'backs to the wall' order. This crisis essentially forces the Allies into something they really hadn't done before: true unity. They appointed French Marshal Ferdinand Foch as Generalissimo.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: The Origins of the Korean War
items.reason: The video erroneously states that Syngman Rhee spent decades campaigning for independence from America (instead of Japan), which is a serious factual error that would lose marks in an exam.

mark_affecting.quote: a fiercely anti-communist exile who had spent decades campaigning for independence from America

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: The Invasion of Kuwait, August 1990
items.reason: The video incorrectly attributes the declaration of Kuwait as Iraq's '19th province' to 8 August rather than 28 August 1990, which directly contradicts the corrected lesson key facts and would cause students to fail lesson knowledge check questions.

mark_affecting.quote: By August 8th, he went from limited coercion to full-blown annexation. He literally erased Kuwait from the map, declaring it the 19th province of Iraq.

items.subject: drama-aqa
items.title: Performance Interpretation: Bob's Final Tableau
items.reason: The video states that Mark's revelation takes place in the summer scene rather than winter, which is a factual error regarding the play's core four-season structure.

mark_affecting.quote: Let's break down that incredibly complex summer scene where Mark reveals to his parents that he's transitioning to Mia.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: The Citizen and the State: A Thematic Toolkit, c1170-Present
items.reason: The video teaches the wrong exam paper structure, claiming there is a 4-mark comparison question and an 8-mark development question, while omitting the compulsory 8-mark source utility question.

mark_affecting.quote: First, the 4-mark question. It asks for two ways things are similar or different... Third, the 8-mark development question.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: The Peasants' Revolt, 1381
items.reason: The video presents the storming of the Tower and beheading of Sudbury as occurring on June 13 before the Mile End meeting on June 14, and repeats the outdated figure of 150 executions instead of at least 1,500.

mark_affecting.quote: June 13th, Wat Tyler's men cross London Bridge ... Step 3 ... they actually storm the Tower of London itself ... The mob dragged out Archbishop Simon Sudbury ... along with Robert Hales, the Treasurer ... dragged out, beheaded
Roughly 150 of the rebel ringleaders were hunted down and executed.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: The English Revolution: Civil War, Regicide and Republic, 1642-1660
items.reason: The video repeats the debunked claim that Rainsborough's specific language directly inspired the Chartists, teaching a false historical fact about the transmission of the Putney Debates (which were lost until 1890).

mark_affecting.quote: that specific language is going to echo through history, inspiring reformers like the Chartists, and the suffragettes centuries later.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Anti-Slavery, Anti-Corn Law, and Reform Campaigners, c1780-1846
items.reason: F15 presents a fabricated quotation and claims Peel attributed repeal to outside pressure rather than any MP, directly contradicting Peel's famous speech singling out MP Richard Cobden.

mark_affecting.quote: The League's campaign, more than any MP, moved me.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Synthesis: Factors Across 850 Years — Cracking the 16-Mark Essay
items.reason: The video states that the Battle of Bouvines took place in 1215 rather than 1214, teaching an incorrect date for an examined turning point leading to Magna Carta.

mark_affecting.quote: War is decisive at highly specific explosive moments, like Bouvines in 1215...

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: From Booth and Rowntree to the Liberal Reforms 1900-1914
items.reason: The video incorrectly states that Rowntree found 21% of York's population living below the poverty line instead of 28%, which is a key examinable statistic in the AQA specification.

mark_affecting.video_says: 21% of York's population was in the exact same condition
mark_affecting.lesson_says: Poverty: A Study of Town Life showed 28% of York's population in the same condition

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Medieval Migrants: Hanseatic Merchants, Jews & Lombards
items.reason: The video explicitly frames and teaches section 5 around an incorrect '4-mark comparison question' (both voiced and on slides at 01:07, 07:02, and 07:18), whereas the AQA GCSE comparison question is worth 8 marks, leading students to write inadequate 4-mark responses.

mark_affecting.quote: Finally, section five: comparing migrations, acing the four-mark question. You need to ace the four-mark comparison question...

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Expansion in India: Company to Crown
items.reason: The video presents Oudh as being annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse rather than for alleged misgovernment, a key distinction required by GCSE examiners.

mark_affecting.quote: Take the Doctrine of Lapse, introduced by Lord Dalhousie. From 1848 to 1856, this policy allowed the company to just annex any Indian state whose ruler died without a natural-born male heir... The final straw was the 1856 annexation of Oudh.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: The End of Empire: Wars, Suez & Independence
items.reason: The video repeats the stale claim that Britain owed the US four years of national income in 1945 (F40), which teaches a grossly inaccurate economic fact that featured in the lesson mark scheme.

mark_affecting.quote: They owed the US four entire years' worth of their national income.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Windrush, Commonwealth Migration & the Legacy of Empire
items.reason: The video includes mark-affecting chronological and causal errors regarding the 1948 Nationality Act, Claudia Jones's founding of the West Indian Gazette, and the Windrush scandal facts.

mark_affecting.quote: Passed just three weeks before the Windrush arrived, the 1948 British Nationality Act...
Right after the Notting Hill attacks, she founded the West Indian Gazette...
Back in 2017, the Home Office destroyed the original landing card archives... At least 164 people were illegally removed...

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Britain & Europe: From EEC to Brexit
items.reason: The video incorrectly claims Polish-born residents were the largest non-UK-born group in the 2011 census (India was first, Poland second) and that immigration was the single most important issue for Leave voters (sovereignty was first at 49%, immigration second at 33%).

mark_affecting.quote: Polish-born residents were the largest non-UK-born group in the entire country.
polling consistently showed that immigration was the single most important issue for Leave voters.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Castles: Instruments of Conquest and Control
items.reason: The video explicitly claims there were roughly 50 castles in England in 1066 (confusing pre-conquest England with the 1086 Domesday survey), teaching students an incorrect figure that contradicts the specification's core point that pre-1066 England had only a handful of castles.

mark_affecting.quote: In 1066, there were roughly 50 castles in all of England. By 1100, that number had exploded to approximately 500.

items.subject: history-aqa
items.title: Monasticism, Learning and the Investiture Controversy
items.reason: The video mistakenly dates the Rebellion of 1088 against William II as 1078, which would lose marks on a GCSE exam.
